stem: A promissory note will pay Rs 13,310 exactly 3 years from today. If the discount rate is 10% per annum compounded annually, what is the present value of this note today?  [Given: (1.1)^3 = 1.331]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Taking the face value of Rs 13,310 as the present value ignores discounting entirely; money received in the future is worth less today.
Discounting for only 2 years instead of 3 gives 13310 / (1.1)^2 = 13310 / 1.21 = Rs 11,000, a one-period error.
Dividing Rs 13,310 by 1.1 x 3 (simple multiplication instead of compound power) gives an erroneous value near Rs 9,000.

explanation: The present value of a single future amount is PV = FV / (1+i)^n. With FV = Rs 13,310, i = 0.10, n = 3: PV = 13310 / 1.331 = Rs 10,000.

explanation_sections.punchline: Divide the future cash flow by (1+i)^n to find its current worth - compounding in reverse.
explanation_sections.lesson: PV = FV x (1+i)^(-n): a single division by the compound factor recovers the initial equivalent value.
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Read FV and n, divide by the given compound factor. Trap: option 1 ignores discounting.
